author: ojiudezue
title: URA predictions audited: none is both useful and correct; anomaly sensor rebuilt on a dwell model
summary: URA predictions audited: none is both useful and correct; anomaly sensor rebuilt on a dwell model
why: Operator plans to use predictions for advanced behaviour but 'they need to be right'. Audit (AUDIT_predictions_room_zone_house_2026_10_21.md): next-room no better than always-guess-usual-room, room forecasts AUC 0.605 ~ constant, '94%' accuracy = empty-room base rate, energy forecasts worse than yesterday-persistence. Root cause: the Bayesian model counts arrivals not dwell, ignores current room, scorers have no trivial baseline. Operator chose rebuild over retire for the anomaly sensor, sensor-only (no alert), and to build first then run the 14-day replay as the live check ('we forget these kinds of cards').
implications: Nothing may consume a URA prediction for actuation until its producer beats a trivial baseline. RoomDwellModel (per-room occupied share by hour x day-type from environmental_data) is the intended shared producer; forecast sensors move onto it next.
revisit_trigger: Post-deploy D0 replay G1-G4 fails at all settings -> retire the anomaly sensor.
